- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong volatility, model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to compensate.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price deviates >3% from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast toward average within 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show downward trend + negative sentiment, model often fails to recognize continuation; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to offset.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to err on conservative side; increase forecast by 0.5–2% to reflect market momentum.
